land.text: Badajoz and the west of al-Andalus (Gharb al-Andalus), from which Ibn Marwan, a Muladi noble expelled from Mérida, rebelled against Emir Muhammad I

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Emirate of Córdoba shapes (757-928) cover this land; this dossier carves it out.

land.text: Badajoz, whose lord 'Ibn Marwan of Badajoz' surrendered to Abd al-Rahman III in 930

successors.note: The Taifa of Badajoz (slug taifa-of-badajoz) arose on the same ground only in 1009.

capitals.name: Badajoz
capitals.note: 'The official foundation of Badajoz was laid by the Muladi nobleman Ibn Marwan, around 875'; 'the seat of an effective autonomous rebel state'.

correction.text: Badajoz and the western march: the province of Badajoz and the district of Portalegre, with the castle of Marvão built in 876-877; the page says only that he 'established his rule throughout Gharb al-Andalus'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row; the Emirate of Córdoba shapes carry the land. The pages name Badajoz, Mérida, Marvão and Coimbra and give no boundary or area; the two-province reading is rough and soft, and Coimbra (expelled the Banu Danis with Sa'dun al-Surunbaqi, undated) is left out.

ledger.note: c. 875: Ibn Marwan founds Badajoz as the seat of a rebel state. 'The official foundation of Badajoz was laid by the Muladi nobleman Ibn Marwan, around 875', after he was expelled from Mérida; 'Under Ibn Marwan, the city was the seat of an effective autonomous rebel state which was quenched only in the 10th century.' He had rebelled against Emir Muhammad I in 868 (Ibn Marwan page).

region.text: the Castle of Marvão, built between 876 and 877

ledger.note: 876-877: 'Between 876 and 877 he also erected the Castle of Marvão', in present-day Portugal; dated at the end of the span. Gazetteer has no Marvão, so Portalegre stands in.

region.text: Badajoz, surrendered to Abd al-Rahman III

ledger.note: 930: 'he achieved the surrender of Ibn Marwan of Badajoz in 930' (Abd al-Rahman III page); Ibn Marwan page: 'His dynasty lasted until 930.' The Caliphate dossier books the matching gain under the string 'Ibn Marwan of Badajoz'.

region.text: Badajoz, passed to the Caliphate of Córdoba

ledger.note: 930: the Banu Marwan's rebel state ends.

wars.name: Revolt of Ibn Marwan
wars.outcome: Ibn Marwan rebelled in 868, won honourable surrender terms after prolonged resistance, was expelled from Mérida, founded Badajoz c. 875 and, with Alfonso III of León sending auxiliary troops, defeated an Emirate army; the dynasty lasted until its lord surrendered to Abd al-Rahman III in 930.
wars.note: The years of the Alfonso III aid and of the flight to Karkar (near Lamego) are not on the page. Abd al-Rahman III's page dates the summer 915 campaign on Mérida to 915 ('his main objective being the city of Mérida'); it does not say who held it. [Reviewer eu-12-x, 2026-10-25: from moved 868 -> 875, the state's start, so the war lies inside the life; Ibn Marwan rebelled in 868 (Ibn Marwan page), before Badajoz was founded c. 875]

certainty.note: The pages name towns and the 'throughout Gharb al-Andalus'; no boundary.

sources.title: Ibn Marwan al-Jilliqi
sources.note: Revolt of 868, Marvão 876-877, Alfonso III's aid, 'throughout Gharb al-Andalus', dynasty to 930; no infobox, no 875.

sources.title: Badajoz
sources.note: Foundation by Ibn Marwan 'around 875', an effective autonomous rebel state; Taifa of Badajoz 1021 or 1031.

sources.title: Abd al-Rahman III
sources.note: Surrender of Ibn Marwan of Badajoz in 930; Mérida the objective in summer 915; no 928/929 Badajoz event.

notes: Written for eu-12-x (suggested by eu-12-a as banu-marwan-of-badajoz, for 900/922-930); three pages. Start 875 is the Badajoz page's 'around 875'; the Ibn Marwan page gives no founding year and dates only the 868 revolt, the Marvão castle (876-877) and the end (930). The man died c. 889 and his 'dynasty' (grandson Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, mentioned on the Abd al-Rahman III page around 913) held Badajoz to 930; no ruler list was opened, so rulers are omitted. Not settled: the extent (Badajoz province and Portalegre district are a reading of 'Gharb al-Andalus'); who held Mérida in 915; whether the Badajoz lords paid the emir between 889 and 930. Disagreement: Badajoz page, Taifa of Badajoz from 1021 or 1031; the existing taifa-of-badajoz dossier starts 1009. The Caliphate of Córdoba dossier uses the counterpart string 'Ibn Marwan of Badajoz' for the 930 gain, which a reconciler should map to this slug; the Emirate of Córdoba dossier has no matching 875 loss (not checked). Gazetteer: admin1 Badajoz and Portalegre exist; Marvão is not a place there.
